why: The job is narrow and the alternatives are all wider than the job. A consumer repository needs to answer one question, 'where on this machine is the harness whose gate I am about to run', and it needs to answer it identically on WSL, on Windows, and on a GitHub runner that has neither. Every off-the-shelf answer solves that by MOVING A COPY of the harness into the consumer (submodule, subtree, vendored directory, installed package), which is a different and more expensive contract: it pins a tree rather than pointing at one, and it makes the consumer carry a second checkout of a 100-file tool tree that changes several times a day. The property this module is built around is the opposite one, stated in its own docstring: a pinned sha here is a MARKER, not a LOCK. Drift fails `check()` and deliberately does not fail `resolve()`, because a product must still be able to run its gate against a harness that moved ahead, and refusing to resolve would turn a stale pin into an outage. No packaging tool has that shape; a submodule at the wrong sha gives you the wrong gate, and a package resolution failure gives you no gate. The second property is the refusal to fall through: a wrongly set `$CLAUDE_HARNESS` raises rather than trying the next candidate, because this estate has already been bitten twice on one day by a lookup that returned a plausible empty answer (`tools/lib/envload.py` returned no .env paths and every caller silently had no API keys; `tools/bus/bus.py` LANE_MAP derived lane '?' for every live checkout because its only surviving entry named a directory deleted that morning). The whole module is 301 lines including a 67-line docstring, and the resolution logic proper is about 50.

alternatives.name: git submodule (declared in .gitmodules), the option this repository's own repo-topology rule explicitly sanctions
alternatives.covers: first-party, no new tooling, and it is the standard answer to 'my project depends on another repository at a known revision'. It gives an exact pin, a single `git submodule update --init` bootstrap, and CI checkout support via `submodules: true` on actions/checkout. It would remove the resolver entirely: the harness would simply be at a fixed relative path inside every consumer.
alternatives.gap: it converts a pointer into a copy, and the pin from a marker into a lock. Running a consumer's gate against a harness that has moved ahead then requires committing a submodule bump in the consumer, which is exactly the friction `.harness-ref` was written to avoid; the ref file's own comment says 'expect drift to be normal'. It also cannot express the live-tree case: this machine has three real harness locations (`/home/shov/work/repos/claude-setup`, a symlink at `/home/shov/claude-setup` that tooling names, and a genuinely separate Windows checkout at `/mnt/c/Users/shova/claude-setup`), and a submodule is one directory. Second gap, measured rather than argued: `repo-topology.md` bans a `.git` inside another repo's working tree except as a declared submodule, so adopting this is legal but it puts a second `.git` in each of two consumers for a path lookup.
alternatives.cost: zero install. Real cost is a full second checkout of claude-setup inside new-recruit and daily-deep-learning, plus a bump commit in each consumer every time the harness changes.
alternatives.maturity: git submodules are as mature as git. Not the risk. NOT VERIFIED: I did not measure how often the harness sha would have to be bumped in practice, only that the current pin drifted eight days (9d94efb5 against 98bb64da) before this session re-pinned it, which is evidence that a lock would have been stale for eight days and a marker was not.

alternatives.name: an installable Python package (uv workspace / `uv add --editable ../claude-setup`, or `pip install git+https://...`)
alternatives.covers: the correct language-native answer, and the one that would make `import harness` unnecessary because the tools themselves would be importable. uv workspaces resolve sibling members by relative path with no absolute path in the lockfile, and `python -m claude_setup.gate` would replace `python tools/harness.py exec gate/gate.py`. It subsumes the whole module.
alternatives.gap: `tools/` is not a package today: no `pyproject.toml`, no `__init__.py`, no console entry points, and 25 `sys.path.insert` calls doing by hand what packaging would do. That is not an accident of this component, it is open scope item S1 in docs/analysis/2026-08-09-session-scope-ledger.md, and it is contested (whether the `intent-control-plane` boundary survives at all is an operator question). Second gap, and the reason this does not become obviously right the moment S1 lands: a non-workspace editable install records an ABSOLUTE path in the consumer's venv (`__editable__*.pth`), which is the machine-naming defect this module removes, moved one indirection deeper and made invisible because it now lives in a generated file nobody reads. A uv workspace avoids that but requires the consumers to be workspace members, which for two separate remotes means either a monorepo or a path dependency that names a relative location, and the consumers do not sit at a fixed relative offset from each other.
alternatives.cost: a pyproject and a package layout for a 100-file tool tree, plus a resolution of the contested boundary. Weeks of the open S1 item, not an afternoon.
alternatives.maturity: uv workspaces are documented and current. This is the alternative most likely to overturn the verdict, and the recheck below is written to catch exactly that.

alternatives.name: environment variable only, with direnv or mise for ergonomics
alternatives.covers: the simplest correct option, and the honest baseline: `$CLAUDE_HARNESS` alone already answers the question, and it is leg one of this module. A `.envrc` per consumer would set it on cd, so the human never types it, and the resolver collapses to `os.environ['CLAUDE_HARNESS']` plus an assert.
alternatives.gap: nothing is then recorded IN the repository. A fresh clone on a new machine, or a CI runner, or a subagent whose shell did not inherit the parent environment, gets an ImportError or a path that does not exist, and the failure names nothing. The `.harness-ref` file exists so the answer is committed and reviewable, and so the error message can list every candidate that was tried. direnv also is not installed on this machine and would be a per-machine setup step in an estate whose recurring defect class is exactly 'a step that requires someone to remember never ran'.
alternatives.cost: zero install if the env var is set by hand; direnv is a per-machine install plus a shell hook, and does not exist on the Windows side.
alternatives.maturity: direnv and mise are both mature. NOT VERIFIED: I did not test whether direnv's environment survives into a Claude Code hook subprocess, which is the case that matters most here and the one most likely to fail silently.

alternatives.name: vendoring, by git subtree or a plain copy at tools/vendor/claude-setup
alternatives.covers: no resolution problem at all: the harness is in the tree. Works offline, works on any host, needs no env var and no ref file, and CI gets it for free from the normal checkout.
alternatives.gap: copy drift, which is the failure this whole estate measures elsewhere: `tools/audit/skills_sync.py` exists solely because a committed copy and a live tree diverged, and the current drift count is 15 across three trees. A vendored harness would add a fourth and fifth copy. It is nevertheless kept as the LAST leg of the resolution order precisely because it is the only one that works with no network and no configuration, which is the right shape for a last resort.
alternatives.cost: disk, plus a sync obligation nobody owns.
alternatives.maturity: not a maturity question. Already implemented as the final fallback.

alternatives.name: monorepo: put the consumers and the harness in one repository
alternatives.covers: the repo-topology rule's own stated default ('one umbrella repo per initiative, subprojects are folders'), and it dissolves the problem rather than solving it. Relative paths always work, one clone, one CI checkout, path-triggered pipelines per subproject.
alternatives.gap: the consumers are separate products with separate remotes, and one of them cannot be merged in for a reason recorded in memory rather than taste: claude-setup carries 295 files with former-employer identifiers and cannot be made public, while the consumers have different exposure. Merging trees merges those constraints. This is the strongest alternative on engineering grounds and it loses on a constraint outside engineering.
alternatives.cost: a repository migration across three products.
alternatives.maturity: n/a. NOT VERIFIED: I did not re-check the 295-file identifier count this session; it is quoted from the existing memory record and could have moved.

alternatives.name: an upward-search library (find-up style), for the self-detection leg specifically
alternatives.covers: `_own_harness()` is textbook find-up: walk `Path(__file__).resolve().parents` until a marker exists. Node has `find-up` and `pkg-dir`; Python has `pyprojroot` and `rootpath` on PyPI doing the same for project roots.
alternatives.gap: the leg is six lines and has no dependency today. Adding a PyPI dependency to a module whose entire selling point is that it runs from the standard library on three hosts would be a net loss. Noted here because the record should say when a wheel was reinvented, and this one was, deliberately and at a cost of six lines.
alternatives.maturity: pyprojroot is real and published. NOT VERIFIED: I did not check its release cadence, because the size comparison settles it either way.

evidence: Read in full: tools/harness/harness.py:1-301 (including the 67-line docstring and all four resolution legs) and tests/test_harness_resolver.py:1-109 (9 tests, including the two that encode bugs the promotion itself introduced: a hardcoded parent.parent that pointed one directory short, and a self leg that swallowed the ref leg for an explicit product_root). Read: /home/shov/work/repos/daily-deep-learning/.harness-ref (written this session), new-recruit's .harness-ref (re-pinned this session from 9d94efb5 to 98bb64da, an eight-day drift), AGENTS.md:80-104 (the consumer-facing contract), ~/.claude/rules/repo-topology.md (the submodule and monorepo constraints quoted above), docs/analysis/2026-08-09-session-scope-ledger.md S1 (the packaging item this record defers to). Ran locally: `python -m pytest tests/test_harness_resolver.py -q` and `python tools/harness/harness.py info`. Line count from `python tools/map/codemap.py prior-art`, which reported the component at 301 lines and is what made this record due. NOT VERIFIED, stated plainly: I did not build a pyproject for tools/ to measure what a packaged version would actually cost; I did not install or test direnv, and specifically did not test whether a direnv-set variable reaches a Claude Code hook subprocess; I did not measure submodule bump frequency, only the one observed eight-day drift; I did not re-count the 295 employer-identifier files that block the monorepo option.
recheck: Any ONE of these re-opens the verdict. (1) `test -f pyproject.toml && grep -q 'tool.uv.workspace' pyproject.toml` at this repository's root: if tools/ becomes an installable package (open item S1), the packaging alternative subsumes this module and the resolver should shrink to an entry point. (2) `python tools/audit/skills_sync.py check` style drift counting applied to consumers: if a THIRD consumer appears and invents its own resolution again, the interface is not being found, and the fix is publishing rather than documenting. (3) `git -C . log --oneline -- tools/harness | wc -l`: if this file starts changing weekly, the pointer has become a copy in disguise. (4) Re-read repo-topology.md: if the monorepo constraint is lifted (the employer-identifier blocker resolved), the monorepo option wins outright and this component should be deleted, not maintained.
what_ours_does: 301 lines, of which 67 are the docstring and roughly 50 are the resolution proper; the rest is a ref-file parser, a sha comparison, and a four-verb CLI. resolve() returns (harness_root, source) or raises HarnessNotFound, never a quiet third answer. Four legs in fixed order. (1) `$CLAUDE_HARNESS`: if set and wrong, RAISE, do not fall through, because an explicit override that is silently ignored is worse than a crash and is the specific failure the module exists to prevent. (2) self-detection, added 2026-08-09 when the file was promoted from a consumer into the producer: `_own_harness()` walks `Path(__file__).resolve().parents` for the marker, so a copy living inside a harness answers 'me' instead of asking a harness to locate a harness. It is skipped when the caller names an explicit product_root, because that caller is asking where THAT product finds its harness, and its ref file is the answer; that guard exists because the first run without it returned this repository via 'self' and never opened the ref file just written for daily-deep-learning, which killed the ref leg for every consumer at the moment the resolver moved. (3) `.harness-ref` at the product root: a comment-tolerant key=value file where `path` may repeat and order is search order, plus optional `repo` and `sha`. (4) a vendored copy at tools/vendor/claude-setup. The marker for 'is this a harness' is `tools/gate/gate.py` being a real file, deliberately an entry point rather than a marker file, because a marker file can be copied somewhere useless and an entry point cannot. check() is the separate verb a gate step calls: it resolves, then compares the pinned sha against `git rev-parse HEAD` of the resolved tree, returns False on drift, and returns True with an explanatory string when the tree is not a git checkout so the pin is unverifiable. Drift fails check() and does NOT fail resolve(). The CLI is `path`, `check`, `info`, and `exec <tool-relative-path> [args]`, the last of which is the form quality-contract.json uses so a domain command can name a harness tool without naming a machine, replacing the `python C:/Users/shova/claude-setup/tools/review/panel.py` that a 2026-07-26 spec named as the decisive architectural defect.
strongest_counterargument: This is a path lookup with a 67-line essay attached, and the essay is doing more work than the code. Three of the four legs are arguably dead weight: nothing vendors the harness, so leg four has never fired; the self leg exists only because the file moved, and it introduced a bug on its first run; and if `$CLAUDE_HARNESS` were simply set in each consumer's environment, legs two through four would never be reached. What remains that is genuinely load-bearing is the raise-instead-of-fall-through rule, which is four lines. The deeper objection is that the whole design is a workaround for tools/ not being a package. Every mature ecosystem solved 'find my dependency' with packaging, not with a bespoke search order, and this repository knows that: S1 in the scope ledger says tools/ has 100 files, no package, no lint, no types, and 25 sys.path.insert calls, and every one of those inserts is the same defect this module fixes for one specific case. Fixing the general case would delete this file. The counter is scheduling rather than principle: S1 is contested, three directories are waiting on an operator decision, and until that lands the consumers still need a gate today; also the pin-as-marker semantics genuinely have no packaging equivalent, because a version resolver's job is to give you the pinned version and this file's job is to give you the current one while TELLING you the pin drifted. But that is a defence of about 60 lines, not 301, and if S1 lands the honest action is to delete this component rather than migrate it.
